name: 36795-sharegptdecode-qwen3next80bfp8-2gpu
hardware: 2x H100 80GB HBM3 on ONE a3 node (`--gres=gpu:2`), NVLink between the two ranks.
parallelism: TP=2, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism, one vLLM engine. FORCED by capacity: ~77 GiB of weights plus the engine's workspace does not fit one 80 GB card, and TP=2 is the smallest topology on this node that holds the checkpoint (~38.5 GiB per rank).
architecture: Qwen3NextForCausalLM: 80B total / ~3B active hybrid decoder, 48 layers, every layer a 512-expert top-10 MoE, FP8 e4m3 block-quantised at [128,128]; ~77 GiB over 8 shards. Geometry is declared in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=16, warmup 5% by completion, bounded at 1000 requests with an 1800 s safety cap -- 50 warm-up requests and 950 measured. The operating point is pinned and must not be walked upward: 16 is a declaration about a low-concurrency serving regime, not a seed to search from.
workload: guidellm `json_file` over `configs/data/sharegpt-1000-qwen3next-out300.jsonl`, single turn, streaming ON, `request_format: plain`, temperature 0.0, ignore_eos true, n=1, no logprobs, no structured outputs. 1000 rows of ShareGPT_V3 first-turn human prompts, tokenised with this checkpoint's tokenizer and filtered to 4 <= prompt_tokens <= 1024 at a fixed 300-token output: mean 218.1 prompt tokens, median 86, min 4, max 1007. Every row pins `output_tokens_count: 300` and `ignore_eos` holds the model to it, so a request costs one prefill step and 299 single-token decodes.
purpose: A conversational assistant on an 80-billion-parameter sparse model, streaming 300-token replies to 16 concurrent users across two GPUs.
launch:
model: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8

# FORCED BY CAPACITY: ~77 GiB of weights plus the engine's workspace does not fit one
# 80 GB H100. TP=2 is the smallest topology on this node that holds the checkpoint.
tensor-parallel-size: 2

enable-prefix-caching: false
max-num-seqs: 16

# Pinned because the default is ambiguous at this commit -- the `vllm serve` usage context
# defaults to 8192 and the in-process one to 16384 -- not because anything is tuned.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

# The longest request this workload can produce is 1007 + 300 = 1307 tokens.
max-model-len: 4096

# Both are the engine's own defaults, written out so a change of default cannot move the
# number between runs.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
enforce-eager: false

# STARTUP ONLY, and it applies to every run. The 8 shards sit on an NFS mount and the default
# loader walks them one file at a time, pulling tensor by tensor out of an mmap; on a 512-expert
# MoE that is thousands of small reads per shard, measured at ~90 s per shard and ~720 s for the
# checkpoint -- longer than the runner's no-progress grace, so the run was killed during load
# before it could serve anything. Measured on this mount: one bulk stream reads 191 MB/s, four in
# parallel reach 588 MB/s, so the limit is per-stream latency and not the link. This reads all 8
# shards concurrently with one bulk read each. It changes only how the weights travel from disk
# into host memory -- same weights, same placement, same engine -- and all of it happens before
# the measured window opens. Expert-parallel is off, so the tensor filter the single-threaded
# path applies is a no-op here and nothing is loaded that was not loaded before.
model-loader-extra-config:
  enable_multithread_load: true
  num_threads: 8

# Deliberately absent: `dtype` and `quantization` (the checkpoint declares its own),
# `trust-remote-code` (Qwen3-Next is in-tree at this commit), and `block-size` -- on a
# hybrid attention/recurrent model the engine DERIVES the attention block size from the
# recurrent state size, so overriding it replaces a derived geometry with a guessed one.
